transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yes, thank you. Well, what brought me in is... I've been noticing that I just keep getting up in meetings, or even at dinner, when everyone else is perfectly fine staying seated. Like, I'll suddenly just feel the need to get up and refill my coffee. 

I actually drink a lot of coffee—usually a dark roast, though my husband just bought me one of those fancy espresso machines for my sixtieth birthday last month. It's a really lovely machine, but honestly, it takes up half the kitchen counter, and trying to find the right beans for it is a whole other project because the local grocery store doesn't carry the ones it needs. 

But anyway, where was I? Oh, right. So I'll get up for the coffee, or if I'm in a staff meeting at school—I teach secondary school—I'll get up to check a handout, or I'll just walk to the back of the room. And the thing is, nothing is really urgent, you know? I just... get up.
Do you feel like you have control over getting up and moving around in these situations?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed or thought about it in terms of having control. It's more like my legs just sort of decide it's time to move, and I just go along with it. 

Speaking of my legs, my knees have actually been acting up so much lately. The stairs at the school are just absolutely brutal. They built the new science wing back in the seventies and never put in a proper elevator, which is just ridiculous for accessibility these days. I had a student last year, Jeremy, who broke his ankle—well, I say broke, it was a really bad sprain from a backyard football game with his older brothers—and the poor thing couldn't get up to my classroom. We had to move all his afternoon sessions to the library on the ground floor just so he could participate. The librarian, Mrs. Gable, was definitely not thrilled about the extra noise, she likes things pin-drop quiet in there. 

But... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Something about the staff meetings?
Do you feel restless when you're sitting in those meetings or at dinner?

Restless... well, yes, I suppose that's a good word for it. Like, when I'm sitting at my desk grading essays, or even when I'm in church, I always catch myself tapping my foot or clicking my pen. I shift around in my seat so much that I literally have to remind myself to just settle down. 

Especially during grading. I'm doing the junior year essays on The Great Gatsby right now, and let me tell you, it is painfully obvious which students just watched the movie instead of reading the book. The newer movie, I mean, with Leonardo DiCaprio. It's a visually stunning film, really—the costumes are just magnificent. My daughter actually found a beaded flapper dress for a themed New Year's Eve party a few years back that looked exactly like something from that set. She bought it at this lovely little vintage boutique downtown. It used to be an old bakery in the 1920s, ironically enough, and they kept the original black-and-white tile floors, which are just so charming. I always mean to ask the owner how she keeps them so clean with all the foot traffic, especially when it snows. 

But... oh dear, I've lost the thread again. Did that answer your question about the meetings?
Do you feel restless all the time, or are there specific times of the day when you feel more restless than others?

All the time? Gosh, I'm not really sure. I haven't really paid attention to the clock when it happens, so I can't say if there's a specific time. Maybe it's just whenever... though afternoons always feel a bit more scattered to me anyway. 

By the time the 3:15 bell rings at school, the hallways are just absolute madness. And the parking lot! Don't even get me started on the parking lot. They hired a new attendant this year, Mr. Henderson, and he wears this incredibly bright neon yellow vest. It's practically blinding if the sun hits it right. It actually looks exactly like the cycling jacket my husband wears when he goes out on his weekend rides. He's been doing these long thirty-mile stretches out by the state park lately. Last weekend he came back and swore he saw a black bear cub near the trail. I told him he needs to be careful, you know, because where there's a cub, there's a mother bear not too far away, and they can be quite aggressive if they feel threatened. We actually watched a wonderful documentary on National Geographic about it just a few weeks ago... it was narrated by David Attenborough. I just love his voice, don't you? It's so incredibly soothing. I could listen to him read the phone book. 

But... oh dear, I'm so sorry. Did I even answer your question? What were we talking about? Something about the time of day?
Do you feel more restless when you're alone or when you're with other people?

Alone or with people? Gosh, I don't know. I've never really thought to compare the two. I suppose it just happens when it happens, whether I'm by myself or in a room full of people. 

Although, speaking of being around people, the staff room has been just so crowded lately. They're doing renovations on the second-floor lounge, so everyone is crammed into the main floor one. It's absolute chaos during the lunch period. And the microwave situation! We only have two, and one of them—the older white one—has this turntable that always gets stuck. It makes this horrible grinding noise. I brought in some leftover lasagna the other day—my own recipe, I use a mix of ricotta and cottage cheese to keep it moist—and I couldn't even heat it up properly because Mr. Davis was microwaving fish. Who microwaves fish in a shared space? It's just common courtesy, really. My mother always said that manners are the glue of society. She was a stickler for etiquette. She even made us take these cotillion classes when we were teenagers, which I absolutely loathed at the time, but I suppose it taught me how to waltz. 

Wait... I'm doing it again, aren't I? I completely forgot what you asked. Was it about being alone?
Do you find that you feel more restless when you're doing something that doesn't hold your interest?

Interest? Oh, I don't know... I really couldn't say if it's tied to how interested I am. I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. 

Though, speaking of interesting things, the sophomore curriculum this year has this new unit on poetry that is just fascinating. We're covering some of the more modern spoken-word pieces, which the kids actually seem to engage with so much better than the classics. I mean, I love Robert Frost as much as the next English teacher, but getting a fifteen-year-old to care about a snowy evening in New England is like pulling teeth. We did have a terrible snowstorm here back in... oh, it must have been 2018. The power was out for three whole days! We had to empty out the entire freezer. We lost a beautiful honey-baked ham that I was saving for Easter. Such a shame, really. I ended up making a brisket instead, which turned out lovely, but it's just not the same as a good ham, is it? My grandmother used to score hers with cloves and brown sugar, and the smell would just fill the whole house...

Oh, goodness. I'm sorry. I've wandered off again. Did that answer your question about being interested?
Do you find that you feel more restless when you're anxious or stressed?

Anxious or stressed? Hmm, I really couldn't say. I've never actually stopped to see if being stressed makes me feel more restless than usual. It's hard to tell, really. 

Though, talking about stress... the state standardized testing starts next week, and let me tell you, the administration has everyone in an absolute tizzy. They want us to cover all the classroom walls with butcher paper so the kids can't look at any of the educational posters during the exam. I spent three hours on a step stool on Monday just taping up this enormous roll of brown paper. I actually ran out of masking tape halfway through and had to go down to the main supply closet, but Mrs. Gable—she’s the art teacher—had taken the last three rolls for a papier-mâché project. They're making these giant piñatas, which is a lovely idea, I suppose, but the mess! There is flour and water paste all over the linoleum in the west wing. 

It honestly reminds me of when my daughter was little and she tried to make homemade slime in the kitchen. She used my good mixing bowls, the vintage Pyrex ones with the little blue cornflowers on the side. I still have that set, actually! They just don't make glass like that anymore, do they? You can practically drop them on the floor and they just bounce. My mother got them for me as a wedding gift back in... oh, it must have been 1986. 

Wait... oh, for heaven's sake, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I completely lost the thread. What were we talking about? Did you ask something about the state testing?
Do you find it hard to focus on one thing for a long time?

Focus on one thing? Oh, I'm not really sure. I haven't noticed if I struggle to focus on just one thing for a long stretch of time. I suppose I just go about my day without really thinking about it. 

But, you know, speaking of focusing, the students have been so distracted lately with the upcoming spring dance. The student council decided on an "Enchanted Forest" theme this year, which is sweet, but they want to string thousands of those tiny fairy lights all over the gymnasium ceiling. The principal is absolutely terrified someone is going to fall off a ladder trying to put them up. And honestly, the gym ceiling is so high! It reminds me of the cathedral ceilings in my sister's house in Denver. She bought this gorgeous A-frame cabin a few years ago. It has these massive floor-to-ceiling windows that look out over the mountains, but the heating bill in the winter is just astronomical. She had to install a wood-burning stove just to keep the chill out. We used to sit around it and drink hot cider when I visited her last Christmas. I brought my famous snickerdoodles, the ones where I roll the dough in cinnamon sugar twice before baking so they get that lovely crackly top...

Oh dear. I've done it again, haven't I? My mind just wanders off. What was the question? Something about the students focusing?
Do you often find yourself switching between different tasks or activities because you lose interest or can't keep your attention on one thing?

Switching tasks? Hmm... I don't really think so. I can't say I've noticed myself bouncing between things just because I lose interest. I usually just tackle my day as it comes, I suppose. 

Though, speaking of tasks, I have quite the list of chores this weekend for my garden. I ordered these wonderful heirloom tomato seeds from a special catalog this year. The company is based up in Michigan, which is just beautiful country. My husband and I actually went up to Lake Michigan for our twentieth anniversary. Oh, the wind off that lake! It whipped my favorite straw hat right off my head and into the water. It had this lovely wide brim and a navy blue ribbon... I was so upset. A seagull actually swooped right down and landed on it while it was floating away! Those gulls are absolutely fearless, aren't they? One of them snatched a French fry straight out of my granddaughter's hand at the boardwalk last summer. Poor little thing cried for an hour, and we had to buy her a whole new cone of soft serve ice cream just to calm her down. She always gets the vanilla with the rainbow sprinkles, though I always tell her the chocolate dip is much better...

Oh, goodness gracious. I am so sorry, I've completely lost track of my thoughts again. What did you ask me? Something about my daily tasks?
Do you feel an internal urge to move when you are sitting still?

An internal urge to move? Oh, I don't know... I really haven't paid attention to whether I feel some sort of urge inside when I'm just sitting. I suppose I don't really sit still all that often anyway, so it's hard to say. 

But sitting still... oh, that reminds me of the faculty meeting we had on Tuesday. We were all crammed into the library, sitting in those awful little wooden chairs for nearly two hours while the superintendent droned on about the new budget cuts. Those chairs are just dreadful on the lower back. I actually brought a little cushion with me, one of those memory foam ones? My daughter bought it for me after I complained about my sciatica flaring up. She got it off the internet, from one of those sites where you can buy practically anything. It’s amazing what they can ship to your door these days. Just last week, I ordered a set of special pruning shears for my rose bushes, and they arrived the very next morning! I have a beautiful climbing rose on the trellis by the back porch—a 'New Dawn', it's called. The blooms are the most delicate pale pink, and they smell just heavenly after a spring rain. I usually go out early with my coffee to check on them, before the neighborhood wakes up and the Miller's dog starts barking. That dog, honestly... a Golden Retriever mix, I think, but he has the loudest bark I've ever heard. 

Oh, for heaven's sake... I'm rambling again, aren't I? I am so sorry, my mind just goes right out the window. What were we talking about? Did you ask about the faculty meeting?
Do you feel more restless in certain environments or when doing specific activities?

Restless in certain environments? Well, yes, I suppose I do. Like when I'm sitting at my desk grading essays, or when I'm in church... I'll catch myself tapping my foot, or clicking my red pen over and over, or just shifting around in my seat so much that I actually have to tell myself to settle down. 

Speaking of church, though, the choir director just announced we're doing a whole new arrangement for Easter service this year. He brought in this guest cellist from the city, a young man who just graduated from Juilliard, I think? Or maybe it was the Curtis Institute... anyway, he plays beautifully. But the cello itself is just magnificent. It's this deep, rich mahogany color, and he said it's over two hundred years old! Can you imagine? Two hundred years. It makes me think of all the antique furniture my grandmother used to keep in her parlor. She had this stunning Victorian settee, upholstered in emerald green velvet. It was so prickly to sit on, though! We were never allowed in that room unless company was over. She kept her collection of porcelain teacups in a glass cabinet right next to it. One of them had hand-painted violets all around the rim, and it was so delicate you could practically see through it if you held it up to the light...

Oh, my goodness. I've completely derailed again. I am so sorry. What did you ask me? Something about grading essays?
Do you think your restlessness might be worse when you're feeling anxious?

Anxious? Hmm, I don't really think so. I haven't noticed if I get more restless when I'm worried about something. I try not to let myself get too worked up, honestly. 

But speaking of being anxious, my neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she's been just a bundle of nerves lately because her son is moving out to California. He got a job with one of those big tech companies in Silicon Valley. Oh, I can't even imagine living all the way out there, with the earthquakes and the traffic. I saw a documentary on television the other night about the San Andreas Fault, and it was just terrifying! They showed these huge cracks in the earth. It was on that public broadcasting channel, the one that always has those wonderful British baking shows on the weekends. I just love watching them make those elaborate cakes with the spun sugar and the marzipan. I tried to make a Victoria sponge once, for my book club, but it came out flat as a pancake. My oven is so temperamental, though. It's one of those older gas models, and the pilot light keeps going out. I really need to call the repairman, but he always tracks mud onto my kitchen floor. I just put down these beautiful new rugs, too, woven cotton ones with a lovely blue and white striped pattern...

Oh, dear me. I've done it again, haven't I? Just talking a mile a minute about nothing at all. I am so sorry. What was the question? Something about Mrs. Gable?
Do you find that you get restless when you're trying to focus on something for an extended period of time?

Focusing for an extended period... oh, I'm not really sure about that. I suppose I haven't paid much attention to whether trying to focus makes me more restless. It's hard to say, really. 

But talking about focusing... that makes me think of my students when they're taking their final exams. You should see them, just hunched over their desks, completely absorbed. Well, most of them anyway. There's always one or two staring out the window. The windows in my classroom look right out onto the faculty parking lot, which isn't very inspiring, I must admit. Though, Mr. Henderson, the history teacher, he just bought himself a brand new electric car. It's this bright, cherry red color, and it doesn't make a sound when he drives it. It's the strangest thing! I always worry he's going to sneak up on somebody in the crosswalk. I read an article in a magazine at the dentist's office about how they're trying to add artificial engine noises to those cars just for safety. The dentist's office... oh, they have the most beautiful saltwater aquarium in their waiting room. The fish are so colorful, like little jewels swimming around. There's a clownfish in there that always hides in the anemone, just like in that movie with the little fish who gets lost. My grandson loves that movie. We must have watched it a dozen times when he came to stay with me over the summer. He's five now, and growing like a weed...

Oh, goodness gracious. I've completely lost the plot again, haven't I? I am so sorry, my brain just takes a little walk all on its own. What did you ask me? Was it about the exams?
Do you feel like you have to move when you're sitting still because something inside you is telling you to?

Something inside me telling me to move... yes, I suppose it feels a bit like that. Especially lately. Since the house got so much quieter after my youngest left for college, I just don't seem to stop. I'll go straight from lesson planning to throwing in a load of laundry, then off to softball practice, and then I'm chopping food for a community event without much pause at all. Even on the nights I promise myself I'm just going to sit down and rest... 

But speaking of that community event, it's a big spaghetti dinner to raise money for the local animal shelter. I was chopping onions for the sauce for what felt like hours! My eyes were watering so terribly. I tried that old trick where you hold a piece of bread in your mouth, but it didn't work for me at all. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable—I think I mentioned her earlier—she swears by wearing swimming goggles when she chops onions. Swimming goggles! Can you picture it? She has this bright pink pair she bought when she started taking water aerobics at the YMCA. The Y just completely renovated their indoor pool, actually. They put in this gorgeous new tile work, all these beautiful shades of aqua and seafoam green. It really reminds me of a trip I took to Florida years and years ago, down in the Keys. We went snorkeling and saw the most incredible coral reefs. The water was so clear and warm... 

Oh, for heaven's sake. I'm rambling again, aren't I? I am so, so sorry. My mind just completely wandered off to Florida. What did you ask me? Was it about the spaghetti dinner?
Do you feel like there's something inside you that's making you want to get up and move around when you're sitting still?

Well, like I was just saying before I got so terribly sidetracked, yes, it really does feel that way. Ever since my youngest moved out for college and the house got so quiet, I just can't seem to stop. I will bounce right from finishing my lesson plans to throwing in a load of laundry, then I'm rushing off to softball practice, and then I'm right back to chopping food for that community event without a single pause. It's just go, go, go. Even on the nights I swear to myself I am just going to sit down and rest... 

Oh, but speaking of sitting down, I just bought the most wonderful new recliner for the living room to help me rest. It's a lovely sage green microfiber, which is supposed to be very easy to clean. The salesman at the furniture store—Arthur, I think his name was—he was so helpful. And he had the most magnificent handlebar mustache! You really don't see those much anymore, do you? It completely reminded me of my grandfather. He used to wax his mustache every single morning while listening to the radio in the kitchen. He absolutely loved those old baseball broadcasts. He was a die-hard Yankees fan, and he would get so worked up listening to the games on that little wooden radio. He had this old hound dog named Barnaby who would howl every time the crowd cheered on the broadcast...

Oh, heavens to Betsy. I've done it again, haven't I? I am so, so sorry, doctor. My brain just took another little vacation. What were we talking about? Was it my grandfather's radio?
Do you feel like there's an internal force driving you to get up and move around when you're sitting still?

I feel terrible, doctor, I must be sounding like an absolute broken record today! But yes, that's exactly it, it feels just like an internal motor. Like I was trying to explain before my brain went on holiday, ever since my youngest went off to college and the house got so quiet, I just can't seem to turn that motor off. I'll be sitting there doing my lesson plans, and then suddenly I'm up throwing laundry in the wash, and then I'm rushing out the door to softball practice, and then I'm right back to chopping vegetables for that charity dinner. It's just non-stop movement, even on the evenings when I promise myself I'm just going to sit in that new chair and rest. 

But speaking of softball practice... those girls certainly don't know the meaning of the word rest, either! They slide into home plate like their lives depend on it. And let me tell you, getting that red infield dirt out of white uniform pants is an absolute nightmare. I actually had to switch to this special heavy-duty detergent to get the stains out. I found it at that little local hardware store on Elm Street. You know, the one with the creaky wooden floors? I just love the smell of that place. It smells like pine wood and cut keys. The owner, Mr. Abernathy, he always keeps a big glass jar of butterscotch candies right on the front counter. He gave one to my grandson when we were in there last month looking for a new hinge for my screen door. That door was slamming so loudly in the wind we had a few weeks ago. It was so windy, it blew my neighbor's recycling bin all the way down the block...

Oh, for pity's sake. I'm talking about recycling bins now, aren't I? I am so, so sorry. My brain is just a pinball machine today, bouncing all over the place. What was the question again? Something about a motor?
Do you feel uncomfortable when you're sitting still?

Uncomfortable? I suppose I do. It's like... well, when I'm sitting at my desk grading essays or when I'm in church, I always catch myself tapping my foot or clicking my pen. I end up shifting around in my seat so much that I literally have to remind myself to just settle down. 

Especially in church! Pastor Miller gives lovely sermons, but last Sunday I was shifting so much I'm pretty sure I annoyed Mrs. Higgins in the pew right in front of me. She actually turned around and gave me quite a look. She always wears these incredibly elaborate hats, you know? The one she had on Sunday was covered in these bright yellow silk daisies. It looked exactly like the centerpieces my sister had at her wedding back in 1985. We had the reception at this lovely little country club, and they served the most delicious stuffed mushrooms. I've tried to recreate that recipe at home a dozen times, but I can never get the breadcrumb ratio quite right. You need a really good parmesan, I think, not the stuff in the green shaker, but the real, aged kind that you grate yourself. I bought a special cheese grater just for that, actually, one of those rotary ones you see at Italian restaurants...

Oh, good heavens. I'm giving you recipes and talking about cheese graters now, aren't I? I am so terribly sorry, doctor. My mind just completely walked away from me again. What did you ask me? Was it about my desk?
Do you think your restlessness might be related to feeling anxious or worried about something?

Anxious? Oh, no, I wouldn't say I feel worried. It's not like a nervous feeling in my stomach or anything like that. It's really just this physical need to keep moving. I don't sit around worrying about things, honestly. I've always been a pretty positive person. 

Like I always tell my students on the first day of school—attitude is everything! I teach tenth-grade history, you know, and those kids can come in so gloomy sometimes, especially right after lunch. They serve this awful square pizza in the cafeteria on Tuesdays. The cheese looks like plastic. I remember when I was in high school, our cafeteria ladies actually made real food. Mrs. Gable, she made these incredible yeast rolls from scratch every morning. You could smell them baking all the way down the science hallway. We used to try to get passes to the library just so we could walk past the cafeteria and smell them. The librarian back then, Mr. Henderson, he was so strict, he would check our hall passes with a magnifying glass...

Oh, sweet merciful heavens. I've done it again. I am so sorry, doctor. I'm talking about library passes now. My brain is just... well, it's just off to the races today. What were we talking about? Was it my students?
Do you think your need to constantly move is related to feeling anxious or overwhelmed?

No, no, I wouldn't say overwhelmed, and definitely not anxious. Like I was just saying, I don't really get worried or nervous about things. It's truly just this... this physical energy in my body that needs to get out. It's not my mind being worried, it's my body needing to do something. 

I've just always been a doer, you know? Even when I was a little girl, my mother used to say I was like a bumblebee, just buzzing from one thing to the next. She had this beautiful garden in our backyard, filled with the most incredible hydrangeas. Huge blue and purple blooms, bigger than my head! She had this special trick where she'd put rusty nails in the soil to change the color of the flowers. It has something to do with the acidity, I think. My husband tried to do that with our tomato plants last year, but I don't think it works the same way for vegetables. We ended up with these tiny, sad little green tomatoes that never ripened. We had to fry them all up just to use them. Fried green tomatoes are actually quite delicious, though, especially with a little bit of remoulade sauce. I found this wonderful recipe in a Southern Living magazine I picked up at the dentist's office...

Oh, dear Lord. I'm talking about fried tomatoes now. I am so, so sorry, doctor. I just... I don't know why I keep doing this. I'm wasting your time. What was the question again? Something about feeling overwhelmed?
Do you feel like something inside you is driving you to get up and move around, or is it something outside, like your environment, that's making you feel restless?

It's definitely something inside me. It's like I have this motor running that just won't shut off, no matter what's going on around me. Especially lately, you know? Since the house got quieter after my youngest, Tommy, left for college... well, you'd think I'd finally sit down and relax. But no, I just move from lesson planning to doing laundry, then I'm off to help coach the girls' softball practice, and then I'm back home chopping vegetables for the church community supper. Even on nights I promise myself, "Susan, you are just going to sit in your armchair and read," I can't do it. 

Tommy's at the State University, by the way. He's studying engineering, which is just amazing to me because neither my husband nor I are math people. My husband is a retired band director. He played the trombone, mostly, but he could play a little bit of everything. We actually met in the marching band in college. I played the clarinet. I always wanted to play the flute, but my front teeth were a little crooked when I was a girl, and the band teacher said the clarinet mouthpiece would be better for my embouchure. I had to wear braces for four years! Those awful metal bands that went all the way around each tooth. Kids have it so much easier now with those clear aligners. My niece just got those, and you can't even tell she's wearing them. She's a cheerleader, so she was very self-conscious about having a metal mouth for the school pictures...

Oh, for heaven's sake. I'm talking about braces and cheerleading now. I am so sorry, doctor. I really try to stay on track, but the thoughts just keep jumping ahead of me. Did I answer your question? Was it about the environment?

doctor.intent: identify the patient's chief complaint
doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Leaving_Seat
target_item.manifestation: What brought me in is that I keep getting up in meetings or at dinner when everyone else is seated, like I'll suddenly need to refill coffee, check a handout, or walk to the back of the room even though nothing is really urgent.
target_item.reason: This is the first turn of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code (S011) regardless of the doctor's opening question.

patient.answer:
Hi, yes, thank you. Well, what brought me in is... I've been noticing that I just keep getting up in meetings, or even at dinner, when everyone else is perfectly fine staying seated. Like, I'll suddenly just feel the need to get up and refill my coffee. 

I actually drink a lot of coffee—usually a dark roast, though my husband just bought me one of those fancy espresso machines for my sixtieth birthday last month. It's a really lovely machine, but honestly, it takes up half the kitchen counter, and trying to find the right beans for it is a whole other project because the local grocery store doesn't carry the ones it needs. 

But anyway, where was I? Oh, right. So I'll get up for the coffee, or if I'm in a staff meeting at school—I teach secondary school—I'll get up to check a handout, or I'll just walk to the back of the room. And the thing is, nothing is really urgent, you know? I just... get up.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's behavior is involuntary
doctor.question: Do you feel like you have control over getting up and moving around in these situations?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about my perceived control over getting up and moving around, which is not directly addressed by any specific symptom profile item (the closest is Leaving_Seat, but I already used that for my chief complaint, and no other item specifically addresses the 'control' aspect of this behavior).

patient.answer:
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed or thought about it in terms of having control. It's more like my legs just sort of decide it's time to move, and I just go along with it. 

Speaking of my legs, my knees have actually been acting up so much lately. The stairs at the school are just absolutely brutal. They built the new science wing back in the seventies and never put in a proper elevator, which is just ridiculous for accessibility these days. I had a student last year, Jeremy, who broke his ankle—well, I say broke, it was a really bad sprain from a backyard football game with his older brothers—and the poor thing couldn't get up to my classroom. We had to move all his afternoon sessions to the library on the ground floor just so he could participate. The librarian, Mrs. Gable, was definitely not thrilled about the extra noise, she likes things pin-drop quiet in there. 

But... wait, I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Something about the staff meetings?

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's behavior is driven by restlessness
doctor.question: Do you feel restless when you're sitting in those meetings or at dinner?

target_item.name: Fidgeting
target_item.manifestation: When I'm sitting at my desk grading essays or in church, I catch myself tapping my foot, clicking my pen, or shifting around so much that I have to remind myself to settle down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I feel restless when sitting in meetings or at dinner, which directly relates to the symptom of fidgeting, squirming, or feeling physically restless when seated.

patient.answer:
Restless... well, yes, I suppose that's a good word for it. Like, when I'm sitting at my desk grading essays, or even when I'm in church, I always catch myself tapping my foot or clicking my pen. I shift around in my seat so much that I literally have to remind myself to just settle down.

Oh, for heaven's sake. I'm talking about braces and cheerleading now. I am so sorry, doctor. I really try to stay on track, but the thoughts just keep jumping ahead of me. Did I answer your question? Was it about the environment?
